Demonstrates advanced level of political and organizational acumen, including experience in maintaining cooperative relationships with schools, universities, community organizations and other institutions.
Experience with program evaluation and development, including thorough knowledge of organizational policies and procedures; understands how work affects the organization and community.

Under the direction of the Associate Dean for Admissions and Student Programs, the Director of Community Engagement and Outreach develops, leads and administers programs that strengthen the School of Veterinary Medicine's engagement with prospective students, educational partners, and the broader community. The position leads DVM pipeline development and outreach initiatives, supports programs that expand access to veterinary career pathways, and develops strategies that foster an inclusive, welcoming, and respectful environment for students, faculty, staff, and residents. The position also provides guidance and resources to school leadership on community engagement, inclusion, access, and related institutional initiatives.
45% - Support of Schoolwide Community Engagement Initiatives
Possesses advanced knowledge of practices and strategies that promote inclusion, access, belonging, and engagement within educational and organizational settings.
Knowledge and understanding of UC guidelines, principles, policies and procedures.
Demonstrates advanced skills in gathering, organizing, and analyzing program data; interpreting findings; and developing and communicating recommendations for program improvement.

Applies excellent interpersonal, active listening, written, and oral communication skills, with the ability to convey complex and sensitive information effectively to individuals and groups from diverse backgrounds.
Skilled in organizational and project management, with the ability to effectively prioritize competing demands, manage multiple projects simultaneously, and adapt to changing priorities.
